newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-FAVRE LEADS PACK TO ROUT OF BRONCOS AS ROZELLE REMEMBERED.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-FAVRE LEADS PACK TO ROUT OF BRONCOS AS ROZELLE REMEMBERED.

text.p: Brett Favre turned what was billed as a possible Super Bowl preview into a rout, leading the Green Bay Packers to a 41-6 victory over the Denver Broncos on Sunday, a day in which former NFL Commissioner Pete Rozelle was remembered around the league.
Favre passed for four touchdowns, including three to Antonio Freeman, as the Packers (11-3) clinched the NFC Central title for the second straight year. Favre leads the NFL with 35 touchdown passes.

Denver, which saw its nine-game winning streak halted, played without star quarterback John Elway, who was sidelined with a sore left hamstring. The Broncos own the NFL's best record at 12-2 and already have clinched the AFC West title and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs.
All of Sunday's games began on a sombre note -- a moment of silence in memory of Rozelle, who died Friday at age 70 from brain cancer.
Rozelle guided the NFL for 29 years before his retirement in 1989, a period of phenomenal growth in popularity and prosperity for the league.
"He always will be the gold standard against which sports commissioners are measured," said current commissioner Paul Tagliabue in paying tribute to his predecessor.
In San Francisco, the Carolina Panthers became the first NFL team to clinch a playoff berth in only its second year with a 30-24 victory over the 49ers.
Kerry Collins threw for 327 yards and three touchdowns as the surprising Panthers improved to 10-4 by beating the 49ers for the second time this season.
Steve Young completed 27-of-41 passes for 391 yards with three touchdowns for the 49ers (10-4), who also clinched a playoff berth, by way of Washington's loss at Tampa Bay.
"They cant be that good, that's not an expansion team I see out there," said incredulous 49ers coach George Seifert.

In Pittsburgh, Norm Johnson kicked three field goals and Mike Tomczak threw a touchdown pass to Andre Hastings as the Steelers clinched their third straight AFC Central title with a 16-3 victory over the San Diego Chargers.
With backup Sean Salisbury starting in place of injured quarterback Stan Humphries, San Diego was held to only 148 total yards of net offence as the Chargers fell to 7-7.
The Steelers, looking for a return trip to the Super Bowl, ran their record to 10-4.

At New England, Curtis Martin and Mario Grier each ran for touchdowns and Ty Law returned an interception 38 yards for a score as the surging Patriots clinched a playoff berth with a 34-10 victory over the hapless New York Jets.
The Patriots (10-4) have won seven of their last eight games to take sole possession of first place in the AFC East.

Martin rushed for 91 yards, becoming the 15th player in NFL history surpass 1,000 yards in his first two seasons. Drew Bledsoe, 24, passed for 251 yards to become the youngest quarterback to pass for more than 14,000 career yards.
In Seattle, Chris Warren rushed for 116 yards and the Seahawks recorded nine sacks in a 26-18 victory that prevented the Buffalo Bills (9-5) from clinching an AFC playoff berth.
Todd Peterson kicked four field goals for the Seahawks (6-8), who scored 20 points off five Buffalo turnovers.
The Seahawks drove Bills quarterback Jim Kelly from the game with six sacks and 12 knockdowns.
At Arizona, Michael Irvin caught eight passes for 198 yards, including a 50-yard third-quarter touchdown from Troy Aikman that rallied the Dallas Cowboys to a 10-6 victory over the Cardinals.
Dallas limited Arizona to a pair of Kevin Butler field goals as the Cowboys (9-5) assumed first place in the NFC East with a one-game lead over Washington and Philadelphia.

In Houston, Natrone Means ran for 67 yards and a pair of touchdowns and Mike Hollis booted three field goals as the Jacksonville Jaguars remained in playoff contention with a 23-17 victory over the Oilers.
The Jaguars improved to 7-7 with their third straight win.
Houston's Steve McNair threw for 308 yards, but was picked off once and fumbled the ball away twice as the Oilers lost for the third time in four games to fall to 7-7.
In Miami, the Dolphins failed to live up to coach Jimmy Johnson's victory guarantee with a 17-7 loss to the New York Giants that took Miami out of the playoff picture.
Giants quarterback Dave Brown engineered two first-half touchdown drives.
"We showed today we are not a very good football team and that is a disappointment to all of us," said Johnson, whose team fell to 6-8 after a third successive defeat.
At Tampa Bay, Trent Dilfer threw a touchdown pass and Michael Husted kicked three field goals to lead the Buccaneers to a 24-10 victory over the reeling Washington Redskins.
Errict Rhett ran for 97 yards and Mike Alstott had eight rushes for 67 yards and one TD for the Bucs (5-9), who have won four in a row at home for the first time since 1982.
The Redskins (8-6) lost for the fifth time in six games after a seven-game winning streak.
In Chicago, Rashaan Salaam ran for two touchdowns and Dave Krieg rushed for a score and passed for another to propel the Bears to a 35-9 victory over the St Louis Rams.
Salaam rushed for 115 yards on 19 carries for the Bears (6-8), who kept their very slim playoff hopes alive.

In Cincinnati, Jeff Blake hit tight end Tony McGee for a one-yard touchdown with 3:09 remaining and the Bengals made a successful goal-line stand in the final seconds for a 21-14 victory over the Baltimore Ravens.
The Bengals (6-8), improved to 5-2 under new head coach Bruce Coslet.
In New Orleans, Bobby Hebert passed for 198 yards and three touchdowns against his former team as the Atlanta Falcons handed the Saints their seventh straight loss, 31-15.
Hebert completed 20-of-29 passes, including scoring strikes to Mitch Lyons in the first quarter, Eric Metcalf in the second and Bert Emanuel in the fourth.

At Detroit, Brad Johnson tossed three touchdown passes and Robert Griffith broke up a two-point conversion pass late in the fourth quarter as the Minnesota Vikings improved their playoff chances with a 24-22 victory over the Lions.
Johnson's 30-yard touchdown pass to Cris Carter gave the Vikings a 24-16 lead with 4:56 remaining.

Barry Sanders, who moved past John Riggins into seventh place on the NFL all-time rushing list, scored from the two as the Lions pulled within 24-22 with 2:34 left. But an attempt to tie the game with a two-point conversion was broken up.
The Vikings have won three of their last four following a four-game losing streak to improved to 8-6.
